name: Buffalo Niagara International Airport
before:
Buffalo's airport, 11 miles east of downtown, and third busiest in New York State. Its catchment of around 9.2 million people is the largest between New York to the east and Chicago to the west.

The reason is across the border. Buffalo is 60 miles from Toronto in a straight line and 106 by road, and it works as a significantly cheaper alternative for travellers in the southern Golden Horseshoe region of Ontario. A good share of the passengers here are Canadians driving south for the fare.

It is a compact site at 1,000 acres with two runways. The airspace above is busy, sitting close to Toronto Pearson, Billy Bishop and Hamilton.

The airport runs its own fire service, which answers all fire and medical calls in the terminal complex from a station completed in 2017, three times the size of the one it replaced.

Signature Flight Support handles general aviation.
after:
Buffalo's airport, 11 miles east of downtown and the third busiest in New York state. It markets itself to Canadian travellers as a cheaper alternative to Toronto Pearson.

The site covers 1,000 acres, with two runways. It has its own fire service, the Buffalo Airport Fire Department.

Signature Aviation runs the private jet terminal.

claims.claim: catchment of around 9.2 million, the largest between New York and Chicago
claims.wasBefore: Its catchment of around 9.2 million people is the largest between New York to the east and Chicago to the west.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia gives it. The operator's overview, about and master plan pages do not, and the master plan documents sit in the NFTA's document search, which lists nothing to a browser.

claims.claim: the reason is across the border
claims.wasBefore: The reason is across the border.
claims.why: A lead-in to the cut catchment claim.

claims.claim: 60 miles from Toronto in a straight line and 106 by road
claims.wasBefore: Buffalo is 60 miles from Toronto in a straight line and 106 by road
claims.why: Only Wikipedia gives the figures; the operator says only that the airport is 'mere miles from the Canadian border and the QEW', and the coordinates check measures from Buffalo, not Toronto.

claims.claim: a significantly cheaper alternative for the southern Golden Horseshoe
claims.wasBefore: and it works as a significantly cheaper alternative for travellers in the southern Golden Horseshoe region of Ontario
claims.why: Softened to what the airport itself claims (see above): the saving rests on the operator's own 2024 fare analysis.

claims.claim: a good share of passengers are Canadians driving south for the fare
claims.wasBefore: A good share of the passengers here are Canadians driving south for the fare.
claims.why: No source from the last 12 months. The operator's page says 'almost 2 million Canadians used our airports last year' but gives no year (its fare analysis is dated March 2025), and no current NFTA figure could be found. For Andy: worth a current figure before this goes back in.

claims.wasBefore: It is a compact site at 1,000 acres with two runways.
claims.why: Reworded without the judgement 'compact'; the acreage and runways are kept.

claims.claim: busy airspace near Toronto Pearson, Billy Bishop and Hamilton
claims.wasBefore: The airspace above is busy, sitting close to Toronto Pearson, Billy Bishop and Hamilton.
claims.why: Only Wikipedia says so; the FAA record carries no such remark.

claims.claim: answers all fire and medical calls in the terminal complex from a station completed in 2017, three times the size
claims.wasBefore: The airport runs its own fire service, which answers all fire and medical calls in the terminal complex from a station completed in 2017, three times the size of the one it replaced.
claims.why: The fire service is kept (operator, FAA). The calls it answers and the 2017 station, its size and cost rest on Wikipedia alone; the operator's news list does not reach back to 2017.

claims.claim: Signature Flight Support handles general aviation
claims.wasBefore: Signature Flight Support handles general aviation.
claims.why: Reworded with the company's current name (see above).
